guides.title: Build typed route URLs
guides.summary: Encode named route parameters without concatenating user input into URLs.
guides.markdown:
Use createRouteBuilder with literal patterns. Ordinary parameters accept strings. Catch-all parameters accept a nonempty array of path segments. The builder encodes each segment. It rejects unknown names, missing parameters and unsupported patterns.

This helper constructs URLs. It does not register routes, authorize requests or prove that a page exists. In an application, prefer the generated route registry when available. Keep authorization on the server. Query state has a separate URL-state API.

guides.title: Capture development navigation and RPC lifecycle evidence
guides.summary: Opt in to bounded navigation, client RPC phases and HTTP server dispatch evidence without storing URLs, arguments or state values.
guides.markdown:
In Vite development code, import startDevelopmentTrace from @cossackframework/core/devtools and call it with an optional capacity (1–2048 events, default 512). Keep the returned session. Read session.snapshot() for versioned lifecycle events and call session.stop() when finished. Calls are not replayed or executed by snapshot reads.

Capture covers framework navigation, component HTTP/SSE and WebSocket proxies, and explicit layout-service HTTP proxies. Narrow by kind (rpc, service-rpc, server-rpc, server-stream, server-socket, server-native or navigation). RPC events share callId and a UUID requestId when available. Component calls have componentId; service calls have a separate opaque serviceId. Service identities do not add service instances or their values to the component snapshot registry. Phases are start, response, state-reconciled and finish. Start means a local attempt, not proof of server dispatch. State reconciliation can skip stale fields and does not prove a DOM commit. Terminal outcomes are succeeded, failed, cancelled, timeout or disconnected. Cancellation does not prove rollback or stop ignored remote work.

No arguments, returned values, state values, method names, routes, provider names or raw errors are stored. Non-UUID wire request identifiers are omitted. A validated stream frame supplies correlation when its HTTP response omitted the request-ID header; later state/terminal events retain that ID. Snapshots are detached. dropped counts evicted events; partial histories must not be presented as complete. Times use the local wall clock and sequence gives event order. Each new session stops the old one; in-flight calls stay with the old session and are not adopted. Stopping capture does not cancel application calls and can leave an unfinished history.

Capture is disabled outside Vite development. The framework browser inspector and opt-in cossackPages({ developmentTraces: true }) Vite bridge consume these snapshots. cossack traces --json and MCP read_development_traces share project-local records with receipt age and live: false; selected values never enter the bridge. HTTP/multipart server-rpc events join the call/request IDs with a separate dispatchId and server receipt/invocation/return/response timestamps. Header evidence alone does not prove body completion. A server-stream terminal joins that dispatch after request cleanup and full RPC stream validation; outcome is succeeded/failed and cleanup is completed/failed. Invalid or missing evidence does not change the call result. Cancellation does not invent server terminals. Browser receipt timestamps and server timestamps use separate clocks. WebSocket server-socket events carry the first yield and terminal frame evidence with callId, requestId, dispatchId, receipt/invocation/return/response timestamps, result kind and frame type. They have no HTTP status or cleanup claim. Invocation/return markers stay null for stages not reached. Browser timestamps mark frame consumption, which can follow a paused queue; server timestamps use a separate clock. The client accepts at most two records for the same call/dispatch and matching frame types. Invalid evidence is ignored, frame limits can omit it, and cancellation does not invent a terminal. Production excludes the encoder and collector. Native server-native terminals travel separately over the opt-in Vite server environment channel after producer cancellation and request disposal settle. They join native response headers by call/request/dispatch IDs without changing body bytes or headers. outcome is succeeded, failed or cancelled; cleanup is completed or failed, including producer cancellation errors. A stalled cleanup emits nothing. Background reporting waits at most one second for Vite receipt, using execution-context waitUntil where available. Headers and EOF do not wait for that acknowledgement, and reports are never replayed. At most 256 recent HTTP correlations and one early terminal per call are retained. A record can arrive before headers or after local finish, but never after capture stop or replacement. Disconnected messages are not replayed. Server cleanup evidence does not prove browser consumption or stop ignored I/O. Development trace acceptance is complete under RT-28. The remaining non-Desktop release matrix is tracked under REL-03.

Navigation events retain navigationId across start/cache/layouts/transition/scroll/finish. Their finish records outcome and committed. component-prepared records an app/layout/page/loading role and the same opaque componentId used by RPC events from that instance. Preparation can fail; it is not proof of a commit or of the cause of every later RPC. Global invalidations and standalone prefetch decisions use navigationId: null. Navigation callbacks retain capture ownership across awaits and stop recording after their terminal event.

Snapshots now include capturedAt and components: a weak registry of at most 64 observed instances. Component records have independent capture times and current lifecycle, initialized public/client state names, passive resource states, scope ownership/counts and transport status. These are current reads, not historical state reconstruction. Values are omitted by default. session.inspect(component, { state: ['count', 'draft'] }) selects up to 32 initialized public/client fields; private/internal/unknown fields stay excluded. Selection returns detached tagged values and is not retained in the event buffer or future default snapshots. Resources are inspected without calling getters or loaders; scope reads do not resolve services. Provider names, cursors, owner URLs, scope keys and raw errors/results are omitted.

State/resource/transport inventories have 64-entry limits; scope ancestry is limited to 16 with at most 64 service slots per scope. Values have a shared 256-node budget, depth 4, 32 object/array entries and 512-character strings. Accessors, unsupported objects, cycles, sparse holes and truncation are explicit markers. Getters and toJSON are not called, but JavaScript proxy reflection can invoke traps; do not select untrusted proxies. Known secret names and common credential strings are redacted, not every possible secret. Select only fields appropriate to inspect/share. Stopping capture stops passive reads. Tracking is unavailable on platforms without WeakRef, while explicit inspect remains available.

Configured deadlines remain active while a component or service iterator is paused after a yield. Timeout/cancellation releases local loading and settles the shared call without another consumer pull. The next pull observes the interruption once. WebSocket disconnects and buffer failure also interrupt paused calls and discard unconsumed frames; already reconciled state remains authoritative. Local terminal capture does not prove that server execution or ignored application I/O stopped.

guides.title: Parse typed URL query state
guides.summary: Read query fields with safe defaults and stable issues. Build a URL without losing unrelated query fields or fragments.
guides.markdown:
A codec converts a query string into a typed value. Define page query fields with defineUrlState and the url codecs. Call definition.read(currentUrl) to get values and issues. Invalid values use their declared defaults. Repeated scalar fields produce repeated-scalar issues. Array fields accept repeated query keys. An invalid array item resets the whole field.

Call definition.url(currentUrl, patch) to build the destination. Unknown query pairs and fragments survive. Declared fields use encoded, normalized values. Defaults are omitted unless defaults is include. A patch value of undefined resets that field. Unknown patch keys and invalid typed values throw UrlStateError. The helper does not navigate, fetch data or authorize access.

Use url.integer for whole numbers and url.enum for a fixed set of strings. URL booleans accept true and false. They do not accept form checkbox strings such as on. Use url.optional when a missing value must stay undefined. Query text, field counts and array lengths have bounds. Custom codecs must be synchronous and must round-trip their serialized values.

guides.title: Parse and type action input
guides.summary: Declare an input schema, infer its raw and parsed types, handle field errors and cancel asynchronous validation.
guides.markdown:
An input schema describes accepted data and returns parsed values. Import input, InputOf and RawInputOf from @cossackframework/core/input. This focused entry also exports parseFormData and validation errors. It does not import components, rendering or runtime adapters. The same helpers remain available from the core root.

Define an input.object shape and await schema.parse(untrustedValue). Use InputOf<typeof schema> for parsed values. Use RawInputOf<typeof schema> for the declared incoming shape. TypeScript types do not validate data at runtime. Always use the returned parsed object. It contains normalized values and does not change the input object. Object schemas reject unknown keys by default. Use unknownKeys: strip only when intentionally discarding extra fields.

Numbers and booleans require their exact types unless coerce is true. Coercion accepts supported strings and rejects ambiguous values. optional permits an absent field. nullable permits null. A missing optional object field stays absent. String fields accept empty strings unless required or minLength rules reject them.

Expected failures throw ActionValidationError. Use isActionValidationError and fieldErrors rather than parsing message strings. Nested object and array errors retain field paths. Root and container errors use the reserved underscore key. Unexpected refinement exceptions remain internal failures.

In a Cossack component, attach the schema through @Server({ input: schema }). Give the method one argument typed as InputOf<typeof schema>. Inbound RPC dispatch parses that argument before invoking the method. Direct local method calls do not run the inbound contract. RawInputOf does not widen a method or browser proxy parameter. Pass parsed values when calling a method typed with InputOf. Parsing does not authorize a user or a record. Apply server authorization before external effects.

A refinement checks a parsed value. It can return a boolean or a promise of a boolean. Pass signal to parse and pass it to external I/O inside refinements. Abort stops waiting for validation and rejects with AbortError. It does not stop I/O that ignores the signal. The examples below prove standalone parsing and cancellation, not a complete RPC transport.

guides.title: Parse and validate nested form fields
guides.summary: Convert bracketed form names into nested records, then apply an input schema before using the data.
guides.markdown:
parseFormData converts bracketed field names into nested objects and arrays. For example, profile[name] produces profile.name and tags[] appends a tag. Numeric bracket keys are object keys. Use empty brackets to create arrays. Repeated ordinary keys also produce arrays. File objects pass through unchanged. Parsed containers have no prototype. A period in a name does not create a nested path.

Read FormData from the request, call parseFormData, then await schema.parse on the result. Form parsing does not enforce field types, array limits, upload limits or authorization. Use input.number({ coerce: true }) for numeric form strings. Use input.file with explicit bounds for uploads. Schema parsing returns typed data or throws ActionValidationError with nested fieldErrors.

Unchecked HTML checkboxes are absent from FormData. Do not assume that the browser sends false. Choose an explicit representation and a schema that accepts it. A malicious caller can add fields or repeat scalar names. Keep unknown-key rejection and handle validation failures before writing data. The executable example parses an array of records and rejects a forged field. It does not make a request or write to a database.

guides.title: Call validated server actions from a component
guides.summary: Use one page for server actions, reactive rendering and browser handlers. Reject invalid input before changing server state.
guides.markdown:
Save the example as a page in a scaffolded Cossack application. It needs the framework Vite plugins and generated client entry. Run the application to execute it. Plain Node execution does not apply the server/client transform.

Extend Cossack and declare the page transport with @Page. State is shared reactive data. ClientState belongs to the browser. Server marks an inbound action. Client marks a browser handler. The security plugin removes server bodies from browser code and supplies action proxies. Browser handlers call the authored method directly and await its result.

Attach an input schema to Server. The dispatcher parses input before invoking the action. InputOf gives the authored method its parsed parameter type. Incoming data remains untrusted, including values sent by the generated proxy. Invalid input produces COSSACK_VALIDATION_FAILED and nested field errors. Validate again at native entrypoints that bypass RPC dispatch.

The example uses HTTP and displays loading state, confirmed count and a validation failure. The invalid button submits zero, which TypeScript permits but the schema rejects. The server owns the count update. Input validity does not establish user or record permissions. Shared State can be supplied by the browser in stateless HTTP calls. Store authoritative balances and permissions in trusted server storage.

Use ClientState for browser drafts and error display. Keep private messages in server bodies. Return only intended public data. Application examples need browser and server acceptance, not only declaration compilation.

guides.title: Load a read-only server resource
guides.summary: Declare server$ data, retain its last successful value, recover after failure and refresh by a typed field name.
guides.markdown:
Save this example as a page in a scaffolded application. server$ is a compiler macro. It needs cossackSecurityPlugin in Vite. Declare it in a Cossack class field or directly inside render. An ordinary function call in Node throws. The loader runs on the server. Its resolved value and dependency arguments are public data.

Keep loaders read-only. Authorize record access inside the loader using trusted request context. Browser selections and dependency values do not establish permissions. Use plain transport-safe objects and finite primitives. Convert database entities and dates to plain data before returning them. Dependencies cannot contain undefined. Use null for an absent dependency.

Use ClientState for browser-owned selections. Declare deps as a callback and return a readonly tuple. Cossack hydrates SSR results and reuses them without an initial duplicate browser request. A dependency change starts a new load. The last successful value remains available during pending and failed loads.

resourceStatus$ returns a snapshot with state, hasValue, value and stale. Render a generic message for a resource failure. Avoid exposing the raw error. A failed browser load does not continuously retry. Change dependencies or call refresh$ to try again. refresh$ retains the last value while loading. invalidate$ removes the invocation and the next read starts from the initial value.

Declare Resources in the Cossack type options to check resource names and values. The example renders an initial record, changes its selection, displays a retained value after failure and refreshes it. It uses derived sample data and does not establish database persistence or authorization.

guides.title: Own asynchronous task results and cleanup
guides.summary: Track reactive inputs, reject stale commits and stop an owned timer when a task reruns or its page is disposed.
guides.markdown:
Save the example as a page in a scaffolded application. ClientTask runs on the browser after mount and when its tracked reactive fields change. Task runs in both environments. ServerTask runs only on the server. The security plugin preserves the required browser handlers and removes server-only task bodies.

Pass the host type to the task decorator and TaskContext to check dependency paths and committed fields. Declared paths must also use reactive State or Store decorators to trigger a rerun. ClientState and ClientStore are browser-owned reactive fields. Methods and unknown fields are not valid dependency paths.

Each execution receives an AbortSignal and a task context. Pass the signal to I/O that accepts cancellation. Use task.commit to replace reactive fields after asynchronous work. It returns false when another execution owns the task or the component is disposed. Direct writes and external effects remain the application responsibility. A signal does not stop work that ignores it.

Return a cleanup function to stop owned subscriptions or timers. Rerun and disposal abort the signal before cleanup. A cleanup returned after cancellation still runs. A retained task context stays current after setup finishes, until rerun or disposal. Commits must contain initialized reactive fields and synchronous data values.

The example simulates work that ignores cancellation. A slow query cannot overwrite a newer fast query because the result uses task.commit. It then starts a timer and returns clearInterval as cleanup. The timer uses the same owned context. The Leave example link requires a root page, which the scaffold supplies. This is browser lifecycle evidence, not a background-job or durable-workflow scheduler.

guides.title: Restore public form input after a redirect
guides.summary: Select public dot paths before a signed flash cookie is serialized. Credentials remain in the server handler.
guides.markdown:
Save the example as src/pages/guidance-old-input/index.ts in a scaffolded application. Configure APP_SECRET for flash signing. A signed flash cookie is readable, not encrypted. getFormData flashes nonempty validation errors by default. It retains no old input unless flash.input supplies an explicit list of public dot paths. flash: true has the same errors-only default; flash: false disables both categories.

Generic flash() rejects the reserved __input namespace; use flashInput for old input.

Use flash: { input: ['name', 'profile.city'] } or call flashInput(data, { fields: ['name', 'profile.city'] }) before redirecting. Selection does not change the parsed or validated server data. Select nested leaves, not whole object branches. Finite JSON scalars and arrays of scalars are copied. Files, Date objects, object arrays, accessors and custom serialization objects are omitted. An array element can be selected with a numeric dot path such as contacts.0.label. Array positions are preserved; unselected positions serialize as null. A later mutation of the source does not change old input.

Known credential paths are excluded even if selected: names containing password, passwd, passphrase, secret, token, credential, authorization, cookie, apikey, privatekey, sessionid or csrf after punctuation removal and case folding; pin, otp, cvv and cvc are also excluded. This is an additional guard, not automatic classification of every custom secret. Keep custom credentials and private values outside the public field list. Keep that policy in server-authored code, not request data. Prototype paths and inherited properties are excluded. Reflective reads can still invoke JavaScript proxy traps; pass ordinary parsed form data, not an untrusted proxy.

Read selected fields with old('name') or old('profile.city') on the following page request. The middleware clears the cookie. Valid incoming flash survives background RPC/upload/realtime requests and failed outgoing RPC writes. The signed cookie carries a server-checked expiry matching maxAge. On Cloudflare, the COSSACK_SSE Durable Object binding consumes each signed nonce once; generated Cloudflare projects include this binding and its SQLite migration. A Cloudflare app without the binding fails closed for flash reads and writes. Node and Deno have no durable replay store, so a copied token remains readable until its signed expiry. Prepare flash before returning a lazy generator. Late writes reject after headers are committed. Do not put secrets into arbitrary flash messages or application-authored validation messages either.

The example submits by native POST, validates email, redirects and restores only three public fields. The password is never restored. It does not create an account or prove authorization. For a server RPC method, apply the same explicit flashInput policy before returning a redirect.
